newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Bakrie Group acquires Elang Realty.
newsitem.headline: Bakrie Group acquires Elang Realty.

text.p: The privately-owned Bakrie Group has taken a 70 percent controlling stake in property firm PT Elang Realty in order to merge two banks belonging to the two firms, a Bakrie official said.
The official, who spoke on condition of anonymity, declined to give details of the acquisition value but indicated that it was above 250 billion rupiah.
He said that Elang Realty would use the proceeds to inject fresh money into Bank Perniagaan, in which the firm owned a majority stake.
The official said Bank Nasional, 70 percent owned by the Bakrie Group, had signed a technical aggreement with Bank Perniagaan to further their plan to merge soon.
"We are now preparing a letter for merger approval from the Finance Ministry," he added.
The Bakrie Group, which controls holding company Bakrie & Brothers, currently operates two banks -- Bank Nasional and Bank Nusa.
Elang Realty had been actively traded since last Thursday on speculation it was a target of a take-over.

In late morning trade on Monday, it was the most active stock on the regular board with 12.8 million shares traded, rising 25 rupiah to 1,000 rupiah, and was up about 14.3 percent since last Thursday.
The Bakrie official said the long-term objective of the merger was to boost assets of the two banks belonging to the group.
He said by the year 2003, the group aimed to operate a bank with minimum assets of 10 trillion rupiah.
"So in the long term, the group will possibly combine the two banks (Bank Nusa and Bank Nasional) through a merger," he added.
